 Why This Position Stands Out
 Yakhyaev enters with the cleaner recent run and the more convincing finishing profile, which helps explain why the market has already made him a clear favorite. The value case is not that Krylov lacks danger; it is that his recent form has included multiple damaging losses, and his style gives a younger, faster starter a real chance to force a fight-ending sequence early. Yakhyaev has been stopping opponents quickly, and the market appears to be pricing him more like a prospect with upside than a fighter with enough live finishing ability to keep clearing this level at a near-sweep price.
For a moneyline position to still carry value this high, the strongest argument is that the current price is likely inflated by Krylov’s name recognition and long UFC résumé rather than by current form. Krylov remains dangerous everywhere, but he has also been hittable and has shown a recent pattern of fights ending before he can settle in. Yakhyaev’s speed, aggression, and ability to create immediate danger make him the side with the better chance to dictate the first half of the fight, and that is where the edge sits.

 Krylov brings elite experience, a long UFC track record, and a finishing game that can punish anyone who overcommits, but his recent stretch has been uneven and includes stoppage losses against quality opposition. Yakhyaev is the less proven name yet the hotter fighter, unbeaten, and riding a run of fast finishes that has translated well to the UFC level so far. The workload gap is also notable: Krylov has absorbed more damage across a long career, while Yakhyaev has been far fresher and more explosive in his recent outings. On current form, the younger fighter looks more likely to impose his pace early and keep the bout in his preferred range.
 Market Trends
 There is no previous head-to-head matchup between Abdulrakhman Yakhyaev and Nikita Krylov.
 Prediction Summary
 Abdulrakhman Yakhyaev is the projected winner, and the most likely path is a submission after he gets the fight to a vulnerable position early. Krylov’s experience and finishing threats keep him live, but the current price still leaves enough room for Yakhyaev to be the value side because his recent pace, freshness, and finishing run make him more likely to win than the market implies. The best position is Yakhyaev on the moneyline, with the projection leaning toward an early grappling-based finish.
